tala.foot: Time = (count − 1) × 60 ÷ laya. By the book Rupak has 14 counts (two gans); the app currently counts a 7-count avartan. The steps of Ektal and Tritaal are not in the book (assumed in the app). Hands: R = right, L = left. Beat: sam = highest, start of a gan = medium, start of a gat = a little lower, other counts = light.
tala.lede: All talas on one time line: every row draws 1 second at the same width. So you can see at a glance where the avartan, the steps, the dhvankar and the anak's hands line up. The first avartan is dark, the next ones lighter. Rest your finger on any count to see its exact time. Press ▶ to hear the tala: a beat on every count — loudest on the sam, a little softer at the start of a gan or gat, the rest light.
tala.leg.tr: Tall line = tankar, short = anutankar; R / L = hand
tala.read.anak: Anak: in talas like Kerva, 4 tankars in a matra, each followed by an anutankar; in Khemta one tankar and two anutankars in each matra, with a light accent at the start of a gat (pp. 52–54).
tala.read.mand: Mandchal: in Dadra 180 one step every second, in Dadra 120 one step every 1.5 seconds. The dhvankar falls on every step.
tala.read.prachal: Prachal: in Kerva, Khemta and Ektal a step falls every 0.5 seconds. Khemta plays three matras in one step, yet its avartan is as long as Kerva's, 2 seconds.
tala.read.sthir: Sthir (standing): the dhvankars of Jhaptal and Rupak fall on every gat, so the gaps are uneven (2 + 3, 3 + 2 + 2).
tala.title: Tala timeline
